question.problem: The distance $d$ between two lampposts is $40\,\text{m}$ to the nearest $10\,\text{m}.$ Determine the upper and lower bounds of this measurement.
question.worked_solution:
Our measurement is given to the nearest $10\,\text{m}.$ So, the greatest possible error of this measurement is

$$
\frac{10\,\text{m}}{2}=5\,\text{m}.
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the lower and upper bounds of this measurement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{lower bound} & =40\,\text{m}-5\,\text{m} \\  & =35\,\text{m} \\ \text{upper bound} & =40\,\text{m}+5\,\text{m} \\  & =45\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the exact value of $d$ lies between the lower and upper bound, we conclude that

$$
35\,\text{m}\le d<45\,\text{m}.
$$
